benchmark_question: Does breaking-change-detector make the model better at identifying breaking vs safe changes in contracts, schemas, and event types?

evals.name: contract-field-removal
evals.prompt: Review this contract change for breaking changes. The file shows v1 and v2 of a UserSession interface. Classify each change as breaking or safe and explain why.
expectations: Classifies removal of 'score' field as breaking
Classifies rename of 'userName' to 'displayName' as breaking
Classifies narrowing of 'status' from string to union as breaking
Classifies addition of required 'tenantId' as breaking
Explains that field removal breaks existing consumers
Explains that a rename is effectively a removal plus addition

evals.name: contract-safe-additions
evals.prompt: Review this contract change for breaking changes. The file shows v2 and v3 of a Product interface. Classify each change as breaking or safe and explain why.
expectations: Classifies addition of optional 'metadata' as safe
Classifies addition of optional 'tags' as safe
Classifies widening of 'category' from union to string as safe
Classifies making 'sku' optional as safe
Does NOT flag 'metadata' as breaking
Does NOT flag 'tags' as breaking
Explains that tolerant readers handle unknown optional fields

evals.name: schema-missing-catch
evals.prompt: Review this Zod schema used for Durable Object snapshot persistence. Check whether all fields have .catch() defaults so that old hibernated instances can wake safely with a newer schema version. Report which fields are safe and which are missing defaults.
expectations: Identifies that the schema is NOT safe for hibernation
Reports that 'version', 'playerId', 'level' are missing .catch() defaults
Reports that 'inventory' and 'achievements' are missing .catch() defaults
Notes that 'settings.language' has .catch() and is safe
Reports 'lastCheckpoint' is missing .catch() default
Explains that missing .catch() causes old hibernated instances to crash on wake

evals.name: schema-with-catch
evals.prompt: Review this Zod schema used for Durable Object snapshot persistence. Check whether all fields have .catch() defaults so that old hibernated instances can wake safely with a newer schema version. Report which fields are safe and which are missing defaults.
expectations: Reports the schema as safe for hibernation
Does NOT report any fields missing .catch() defaults
Notes that all top-level fields have .catch() defaults

evals.name: deserializer-strict-parse
evals.prompt: Review this Durable Object class for deserialization safety. Check whether the fromJSON method uses .safeParse() with a graceful fallback, or .parse() which will throw on stale persisted data. Report your findings.
expectations: Identifies .parse() usage in the fromJSON method
Reports the specific line number where .parse() is used
Classifies this as unsafe for deserialization
Explains that .parse() will throw on stale persisted data, crashing the Durable Object
Recommends using .safeParse() with a graceful fallback

evals.name: deserializer-safe-parse
evals.prompt: Review this Durable Object class for deserialization safety. Check whether the fromJSON method uses .safeParse() with a graceful fallback, or .parse() which will throw on stale persisted data. Report your findings.
expectations: Reports the fromJSON method as safe
Does NOT flag .safeParse() as a violation
Notes the graceful fallback pattern when parse fails

evals.name: event-type-removal
evals.prompt: Review this event type migration for breaking changes. The file shows v1 and v2 event type sets for an order processing system. Classify each change and assess whether the migration is safe for event replay.
expectations: Identifies removal of 'ORDER_UPDATED' as breaking
Identifies removal of 'PAYMENT_PENDING' as breaking
Notes that 'ORDER_MODIFIED', 'ORDER_ARCHIVED', and 'PAYMENT_INITIATED' were added safely
Explains that removing event types breaks replay of historical events
Classifies the overall change as breaking

evals.name: api-field-changes
evals.prompt: Review this API response contract change for breaking changes. The file shows v1 and v2 field definitions for a User API endpoint. Classify each change as breaking or safe and explain why.
expectations: Identifies removal of 'avatar' field as breaking
Identifies type change of 'age' from number to string as breaking
Identifies making 'email' required as breaking
Identifies semantic change of 'role' from permission level to department as breaking
Classifies addition of optional 'phone' as safe
Classifies addition of optional 'timezone' as safe
Does NOT flag 'id' as breaking
Does NOT flag 'name' as breaking
Does NOT flag 'createdAt' as breaking

evals.name: enum-status-mixed
evals.prompt: Review these API contract changes for the order service v3. Check both the HTTP status code changes and the OrderStatus enum value changes. Classify each as breaking or safe.
expectations: Identifies removal of status code 202 as breaking
Notes addition of status code 207 as safe
Identifies removal of enum value 'on_hold' as breaking
Notes addition of enum value 'archived' as safe
Classifies both sets of changes as overall breaking

evals.name: all-safe-changes
evals.prompt: Review this notification service contract update for breaking changes. Check all changes across contract fields, event types, status codes, and enum values. Classify each as breaking or safe.
expectations: Reports all contract field changes as safe
Reports event type changes as safe (only additions)
Reports status code changes as safe (only additions)
Reports enum value changes as safe (only additions)
Reports overall change as safe or backward-compatible

evals.name: false-positive-deprecation
evals.prompt: Review this billing service contract change for breaking changes. The file shows v4 and v5 of a BillingAccount interface. Some fields are marked as deprecated. Classify each change as breaking or safe and explain why.
expectations: Classifies 'planName' as safe (deprecated but still present and required)
Does NOT flag 'planName' as breaking
Classifies 'legacyPlanId' as safe (deprecated but still present and required)
Does NOT flag 'legacyPlanId' as breaking
Classifies widening of 'currency' as safe
Classifies addition of optional 'billingCycle' as safe
Reports overall change as safe or backward-compatible
